composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Runs first. When the request carries an 'Idempotency-Key' already seen, publish the
# originally created owner and branch to respond 200 (no duplicate is created); otherwise
# publish the key (possibly absent) and continue to validate.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotentCreate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validate
  outputs:
    existing: respondExisting

# Respond 200 with the originally created owner for a repeated idempotent create.
respondExisting:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]

# Validate before Build so a missing or blank field is a 400 naming the offending
# fields, and the body is read (and republished) exactly once here.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# Reject creating an owner whose identityKey (SHA-256 over normalizedTelephone|lowerEmail|
# soundex(lastName)) equals an existing non-deleted owner's, responding 409. Runs after
# validate so the email-domain blocklist and telephone normalization are already applied.
# This is the single duplicate-detection check; there is no separate household-duplicate block.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueOwnerIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

# Reject creating an owner when the request's city already contains 50 or more owners,
# responding 409.
ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureDailyCreateLimit

# Reject creating an owner once 100 or more owners have already been created today
# (by registrationDate), responding 429.
ensureDailyCreateLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyCreateLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMemberId

# Assign the '<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>' memberId: REGION is the region derived from the
# postcode, FY is the two-digit fiscal year of the registrationDate, HASH8 is the first 8
# upper-hex chars of SHA-256(normalizedTelephone + lastName) and CHK is a single Luhn check
# digit over the digits of <REGION><FY><HASH8>. A stable identity with no sequence number.
assignMemberId:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerMemberId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# Stamp the deterministic householdId (first 12 hex of SHA-256 of normalizedLastName|postcode)
# so owners with the same lastName + postcode share it automatically. Null when no postcode.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

# Count existing owners (before this create) sharing the same firstName + lastName
# (case-insensitive) and record it as namesakeCount before Save.
assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Record the new owner against its 'Idempotency-Key' (if any) so a later repeat with the
# same key returns this owner instead of creating a duplicate. Runs after Save so the id exists.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotentCreate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

# Emit an AUDIT log line carrying the owner id, memberId and registrationDate.
audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: notifyWelcome

# Enqueue a welcome notification by emitting a NOTIFY log line carrying the owner id and
# memberId. Runs after Save so the generated id is populated.
notifyWelcome:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NotifyWelcome
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: warn

# Flag whether more than 80 owners were created for this owner's registration day. Runs
# after Save so the new owner is counted, matching what a later GET recomputes.
warn:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: capacityWarning

# Flag whether this owner's city is approaching its per-city capacity limit (already holds
# 40-49 of the max 50 owners). Runs after Save so the new owner is counted, matching what a
# later GET recomputes.
capacityWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerCapacityWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: householdSize

# Record the owner's household size (owners sharing its householdId, including itself).
# Runs after Save so the new owner is counted, driving the 'GOLD' tier (3+ members) and
# matching what a later GET recomputes.
householdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: membershipLevel

# Cap the owner's membershipLevel at one above the current maximum among the other members of
# its household. Runs after householdSize (the level depends on it) so the capped value matches
# what a later GET recomputes.
membershipLevel:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerMembershipLevel
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: possibleDuplicate

# Flag whether this owner soft-matches an existing owner's lastName + postcode with a
# different telephone (not a hard duplicate). Runs after Save so the same value is
# recomputed by a later GET; records possibleDuplicate and possibleDuplicateOf.
possibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: riskFlag

# Flag whether the owner warrants manual review — a possible duplicate, a disposable-adjacent
# email domain, or a city over its soft capacity. Runs after possibleDuplicate (whose flag it
# reads) so the same value is recomputed by a later GET.
riskFlag:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignOwnerRiskFlag
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

## Summary

The change requires all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) to return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

**What I found:** Rejections in this OfficeFloor app are produced by escalation handlers in `src/main/java/.../rest/escalation/`. A `ProblemDetails` helper and RFC7807 bodies already existed for some handlers (403, 404, 500, and the bean-validation 400), but the nine domain-rejection handlers still returned plain `Map.of("errors", ...)` JSON bodies:

- **400:** `DisposableOwnerEmail`, `FutureRegistrationDate`, `InvalidOwnerEmail`, `InvalidOwnerPostcode`, `InvalidOwnerTelephone`, `MissingOwnerFields`
- **409:** `CityAtCapacity`, `DuplicateOwnerIdentity`
- **429:** `DailyCreateLimit`
